analysis.title: Memory meltdown: from unstoppable to uninvestable
key_insights: Memory stocks have unwound sharply over the past several sessions. Goldman's memory basket rose from about 600 to a June peak of 2,675 and has fallen toward 1,900, almost 30% off the high.
Samsung and SK Hynix are down roughly 22% and 26% respectively over five sessions.

Foreign investors have sold $11.6B of Korean tech over eight consecutive sessions (Goldman). SK Hynix has had 15 straight days of foreign selling and Samsung five. Domestic institutions and retail are absorbing some of the supply.

Hedge funds have been net sellers of global AI stocks for five consecutive sessions. Net allocation fell to 26.1% from a June peak of 31.7%. The aggregate long/short ratio fell from 4.34 to 3.27, the seventh percentile over the past year.

Equities and physical prices have diverged: DDR5 spot prices keep rising while memory equities fall. Samsung trades at about 1.2x book and SK Hynix at about 0.9x, which Goldman reads as the market discounting a significant downturn by 2028.

China's CXMT announced 4F² technology, raising supply-shock fears. CXMT reached about 10% of global DRAM revenue in Q2, but commercial qualification of the new technology is uncertain and it still faces HBM yield challenges. The note argues the market is treating commodity DRAM and HBM as one trade.

Technicals: SOX RSI is 34 and the index is testing the lower end of its trading range. With positioning reduced, valuations compressed and physical memory prices holding, the note sees conditions for a countertrend squeeze, without guaranteeing a bottom.

sector_views.rationale: The note sees a possible countertrend squeeze after the selloff but says none of this guarantees a bottom.

risk_factors: Further foreign and hedge fund liquidation of Korean memory and AI exposure.
CXMT's progress in conventional DRAM and a possible supply shock from its 4F² technology.
A memory cycle downturn by 2028, which the note says the equity valuations already discount.
Domestic institutions and retail may not be able to absorb more supply.
